discovery: Prediction and experimental demonstration of current-induced spin-transfer torque in magnetic nanostructures
subfield: Condensed matter physics: spintronics and magnetism
motivation: Giant magnetoresistance, recognized in 2007, showed that magnetization controls electrical current. The reverse was the next step: an electrical current can control magnetization. Luc Berger predicted that a spin-polarized current passing through a ferromagnet transfers angular momentum to it, exerting a torque that can switch or drive the magnetization into steady precession. Daniel Ralph and Robert Buhrman gave the decisive demonstrations in nanopillar spin valves. They showed current-driven magnetization reversal (1999-2000), then directly detected microwave oscillations of a nanomagnet driven by a direct current (2003). These results founded modern spin-current physics, which led to spin pumping, spin-orbit torques and antiferromagnetic spintronics. They have been reproduced in hundreds of laboratories. Spin-transfer-torque MRAM is now manufactured commercially by major foundries. This is a fundamental discovery about how angular momentum is transferred in quantum transport, and it has had lasting technological impact.
